Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
705 AM EDT Wed Mar 18 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Cold with below average temperatures through Thursday.

2) No major storm systems through the forecast period, with just
a few minor disturbances late in the week and this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
High pressure builds over the area today, and then slowly builds
off the northeast coast tonight through Thursday. This airmass
brought in colder than normal air with temperatures starting out
in the lower to mid 20s this morning, with highs expected to
range in the 30s, some 10 to 13 degrees below normal. With
nearly clear skies and light winds, radiational cooling tonight
will allow for temperatures to drop back into the mid and upper
20s, near 30 in New York City. Temperatures slowly recover
Thursday as the high moves off the coast, with temperatures
still around 5 degrees below normal.


.KEY MESSAGE 2... 
A couple of weak disturbances embedded in the WNW flow regime 
will progress through late Friday into Sat AM, and Sun and Sun 
night. A cold front passes through Sunday night returning above
normal temperatures of Friday through Sunday to more seasonal
levels. No hazardous weather is expected with these 
disturbances.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR with high pressure through the TAF period.

NW winds around 10 kt or less this morning. Winds will briefly 
become light, possibly variable after 15z, but should prevail 
out of the S or SE under 10 kt after 19-21z. Winds become light 
and variable once again this evening or remain generally light
out of the SSE.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 

Timing of wind shift to the S-SE may be off by 1-3 hours. 

.OUTLOOK FOR 12Z THURSDAY THROUGH SUNDAY... 

Thursday: VFR.

Thursday Night: Mainly VFR. Low chance for rain or snow shower
and MVFR, mainly NW of NYC metro. 

Friday-Friday night: VFR during the day, with possible MVFR or
lower in -RA at night.

Saturday and Sunday: Chance of rain and MVFR. S-SW gusts 15-20
kt possible.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component 
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
SCA conditions gradually subside by early this morning across
the far eastern Long Island Sound. Ocean seas will remain
elevated at SCA levels on the waters west of Moriches Inlet
until late tonight, and through tonight east of Moriches Inlet.
The SCA for the ocean waters was adjusted for the longer period
of SCA seas on the western ocean waters.

Sub advisory conditions then prevail with high pressure 
essentially remaining nearby Thursday through Friday. A
strengthening southerly flow Friday night into Saturday will
bring marginal SCA conditions to the ocean waters toward
Saturday morning, becoming more likely by the afternoon as the
southerly flow continues. Small craft conditions then continue
into Sunday night.

&&
